raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

OpenAI returns errors as `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}`, where `code` is a string or null (`ErrorResponse`). SGLang's OpenAI routes return a flat body with class-style types (`"BadRequestError"`) and the HTTP status as an integer `code`, so OpenAI clients lose the message or fail to parse the error. The open #33534 changes only the non-streamed body.

## Modifications

- **Scope:** the routes that serve the OpenAI API (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/models`, and SageMaker's `/invocations`, which shares the chat serving) now return the envelope:
  - from their servings, including stream error frames;
  - from the `HTTPException` and validation handlers and the API-key middleware.
- SGLang's own routes (`/generate`, score, tokenize, rerank, classify, decisions, systemone) keep their shapes. `/v1/responses` and the Anthropic routes keep theirs.
- **Fields:**
  - `error.type` follows the HTTP status: `authentication_error`, `permission_error`, `rate_limit_error`, `service_unavailable_error`, `server_error`, otherwise `invalid_request_error`.
  - `code` is null except the models 404's `"model_not_found"`.
  - `message` is always a string.
  - HTTP statuses are unchanged.
- **Server errors:** the `serving_base` catch-all 500 no longer includes exception text, on every serving route. An `HTTPException` keeps its detail.
- **gRPC:** errors returned by the chat, completions and embedding servings use the envelope. The bridge's own errors (request parsing, its catch-all) are unchanged; for streamed requests they are gRPC statuses.
- **Anthropic adapter:** it maps upstream stream errors by `error.type`.
- **Rust:** `sglang-processor` and `sglang-server` emit the same envelope; the processor's parity fixtures are updated.

**Breaking change for the OpenAI routes:**
- The flat body's top-level `object`, `message`, `type` and `code` are gone. Clients read `body["error"]["message"]` and the response status.
- `error.type` values change from class-style names to the types above.
- The API-key middleware's `{"error": "Unauthorized"}` becomes an object.
- A stream error frame no longer carries the numeric status, only `error.type`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: response metadata only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Validation

- **Python:**
  - The new `test_openai_error_envelope.py` covers the helper, each status type, the route list, both exception handlers (including `/generate` keeping its shape), the API-key middleware, the transcription and models errors, and which servings opt in.
  - These pass on CPU, with the chat, completions, transcription, embedding, decisions, scoring, systemone, Anthropic and auth suites.
- **Rust:**
  - `cargo test -p sglang-processor --features openai,render,tokenizer` and `cargo test -p sglang-server --lib openai` pass.
- 2026-10-29: rebased onto main `974831643f`, where `sglang-processor` reads typed `/generate` errors and `sglang-server` serves chat through the processor (`lowered.rs`); both now return the envelope. On the new head, `test_openai_error_envelope.py` and the Anthropic, chat, completions and transcription suites pass on CPU, except 5 long-audio transcription tests and 1 Inkling chat subtest that fail the same way on main in this environment; `cargo test -p sglang-processor --all-features` (with the parity fixtures), `cargo test -p sglang-server --lib` and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` pass on Linux.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+def openai_error_type(status_code: int) -> str:
+    """The OpenAI ``error.type`` for an HTTP status code."""
+    if status_code == 401:
+        return "authentication_error"
+    if status_code == 403:
+        return "permission_error"
+    if status_code == 429:
+        return "rate_limit_error"
+    if status_code == 503:

+    if status_code >= 500:

+    return "invalid_request_error"

+# completions). Their errors use OpenAI's error envelope; SGLang's own routes
+# keep their documented error shapes, and /v1/responses keeps its own.

+
+def is_openai_api_route(path: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``path`` (without the root path) serves the OpenAI API."""
+    return any(
+        path == route or path.startswith(route + "/") for route in OPENAI_API_ROUTES
+    )
+
+
+def openai_error_body(
+    message: Any,
+    status_code: int,
+    param: Optional[str] = None,
+    code: Optional[str] = None,
+) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """An OpenAI ``ErrorResponse`` body: ``{"error": {message, type, param, code}}``.
+
+    ``message`` is coerced to a string (an ``HTTPException.detail`` can be any
+    value); ``code`` is an OpenAI string error code (e.g. ``"model_not_found"``)
+    or None, never the HTTP status, which the response status already carries.
+    """
+    if message is None:
+        try:
+            message = HTTPStatus(status_code).phrase
+        except ValueError:
+            message = "Request failed"
+    return {
+        "error": {
+            "message": message if isinstance(message, str) else str(message),
+            "type": openai_error_type(status_code),
+            "param": param,
+            "code": code,

+
+def _handle(exc_type, path, exc, root_path=""):

+
+def _assert_envelope(test, body, message, error_type, param=None, code=None):
